incidents.summary: A union reported that Next's wholly owned subsidiary abruptly closed its Katunayake factory, leaving more than 1,400 workers without jobs through text-message dismissals.

sources.title: Investor webinar highlights mounting labour concerns at Next plc - industriall-union
sources.quote: Anton Marcus, general secretary of the Free Trade Zones & General Services Employees Union (FTZGSEU), described the abrupt May closure of a factory run by its wholly owned subsidiary, Next Manufacturing Ltd (NML), in the Katunayake Free Trade Zone,

sources.title: Investor webinar highlights mounting labour concerns at Next plc - industriall-union
sources.quote: where more than 1,400 workers lost their jobs via text message and were locked out of the factory.

incidents.summary: The Living Wage Foundation campaigned for Next to pay at least £7.65, and the retailer was subsequently criticised for failing to pay a living wage.

sources.title: Next plc
sources.quote: In May 2014, the Living Wage Foundation bought Next shares and attended the annual general meeting in an attempt to persuade the company to pay at least £7.65 and become one of the UK's 700 living wage employers.

sources.title: Next plc
sources.quote: In October 2014, the company was one of several retailers criticised by journalist Janice Turner in The Times for failing to pay what she described as a living wage.

positives: Next temporarily suspended sales of Boohoo and PrettyLittleThing products amid labour-exploitation concerns and began its own investigation.
Next joined the U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol, which provides verified sustainability data for cotton sourcing.
Next's target to reduce emissions by 55% by 2030 from a 2016–17 baseline was approved by SBTi.
